cover.title: Your Explanation of Benefits
cover.specimenLine: Synthetic test document — not issued by any health plan
cover.intro: This statement lists the medical claims {legalName} processed for you during the period shown. It tells you what your providers billed, what the plan approved, what the plan paid, and what you may owe. Keep it with your health records. Any amount you owe is billed to you by the provider, not by us.

info.title: Understanding your statement

definitions.text: The amount your doctor, hospital or other provider charged for the service.
The total cost the plan allows for a covered service. In-network providers agree to accept it as payment in full.
The part of the plan-approved amount we paid to the provider.
The part of the plan-approved amount you are responsible for: a copayment, coinsurance, or an amount applied to your deductible.
A set dollar amount you pay for a type of service, such as an office visit.
A percentage of the plan-approved amount that you pay for certain services.
The amount you pay for certain covered services each year before the plan begins to pay its share for them.
The most you pay in a year for covered in-network medical services. After you reach it, the plan pays 100% of the approved amount for those services.
A provider who has a contract with the plan. You usually pay less when you see in-network providers.

checkItems: Compare the services and dates with your own records and any receipts.
Never pay a provider more than the figure in the Your share column.
If you already paid a provider more than your share, ask the provider for a refund.
info.disagreeTitle: If you disagree with how a claim was processed
disagree: Call Member Services first. Many questions can be answered over the phone, and we can review a claim that looks wrong.

If we decide not to pay for some of your care, or to pay less than you expected, you can appeal. For each such decision we mail you its own written notice with the steps to follow and the date by which you must act.

For free, independent help with appeals and benefits questions, the State Health Insurance Assistance Programs (SHIPs) help people with Medicare; or call 1-800-MEDICARE (1-800-633-4227); TTY users can call 1-877-486-2048.
info.deniedTitle: Services on this statement that were denied
denied: We did not pay for at least one service on this statement; the note next to it gives the reason. You will also receive a written denial notice that describes how to request a reconsideration (an appeal) and your deadline.
fraud: Review this statement for services you did not receive, dates when you did not see a provider, or providers you do not recognize.
If something looks wrong, call our fraud line at {fraudPhone} (TTY {tty}). You can also call 1-800-MEDICARE (1-800-633-4227); TTY users can call 1-877-486-2048.
Never give your member ID or Medicare number to anyone who calls or visits you uninvited.

notices.title: Your rights and language help
nondiscrimination: {legalName} complies with applicable Federal civil rights laws and does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, national origin, age, disability, or sex. {legalName} does not exclude people or treat them differently because of race, color, national origin, age, disability, or sex.

nondiscriminationServices.text: Provides free aids and services to people with disabilities to communicate effectively with us, such as:
items: Written information in other formats (large print, audio, accessible electronic formats, other formats)

nondiscriminationServices.text: Provides free language services to people whose primary language is not English, such as:

nondiscriminationAfter: If you need these services, contact our Civil Rights Coordinator at 614-555-0153 (TTY 711).
notices.grievanceTitle: If you believe you were treated unfairly
grievance: If you believe that {legalName} has failed to provide these services or discriminated in another way on the basis of race, color, national origin, age, disability, or sex, you can file a grievance with: Civil Rights Coordinator, 100 Specimen Way, Suite 410, Columbus, OH 43215, 614-555-0153, TTY 711, Fax 614-555-0154, civilrights@corvane.example. You can file a grievance in person or by mail, fax, or email. If you need help filing a grievance, the Civil Rights Coordinator is available to help you.

You can also file a civil rights complaint with the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Office for Civil Rights electronically through the Office for Civil Rights Complaint Portal, available at https://ocrportal.hhs.gov/ocr/portal/lobby.jsf, or by mail or phone at: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, 200 Independence Avenue SW., Room 509F, HHH Building, Washington, DC 20201, 1-800-368-1019, 800-537-7697 (TDD).
